parsed.label: hypothesis: negative activation for tokens preceding a noun phrase describing a text or speech genre
parsed.trigger_hypothesis: The neuron fires negatively (strong negative activation) when the token is part of a phrase that immediately precedes a noun phrase describing a genre or form of text or speech (e.g., 'love letter', 'first-person narrative', 'Prosopopeia').
parsed.output_hypothesis: The neuron's negative activation may suppress the generation of generic or formulaic text openings, encouraging more varied or specific continuations when a text genre is introduced.
alternatives: The neuron detects tokens that are part of common prepositions or determiners before abstract nouns (e.g., 'of', 'a', 'the').
The neuron responds to the end of a user prompt or instruction, signaling a transition to model response.
parsed.adapter_changes: State C+1 shows a large positive increase specifically at token '\n\n' in prompts (W20-W23), suggesting this state amplifies the neuron's response to newline sequences preceding assistant responses, while other states have minimal changes.
